legionary.name: Legionaries
legionary.text: Two legionaries join the front ranks.
legionary.history: Citizen soldiers who signed up for 25 years, then received land or a pension.

archer.name: Archers
archer.text: Two archers join the rear and shoot the nearest enemy.
archer.history: Auxiliary archers, often from Syria, used composite bows that outranged most tribal weapons.

slinger.name: Slingers
slinger.text: Two slingers join the rear and throw stones that knock enemies back.
slinger.history: Slingers from the Balearic Islands hurled lead bullets that could break a shield.

cavalry.name: Cavalrymen
cavalry.text: Two horsemen ride out at enemies near the flanks.
cavalry.history: Auxiliary horsemen from Gaul and Spain scouted ahead and chased down broken enemies.

standard_bearer.name: Standard bearer
standard_bearer.text: A standard bearer raises the attack speed of every soldier near him.
standard_bearer.history: The signifer carried the unit standard, and losing it in battle was a deep disgrace.

promotion.text: His aura covers the whole legion.

medicus.name: Medicus
medicus.text: A medicus heals the most wounded soldier near him.
medicus.history: Army doctors set bones and stitched wounds, and had a permanent place in the legion.

promotion.text: Revives one fallen soldier a minute.

ballista.name: Ballista crew
ballista.text: A ballista crew fires a heavy bolt down a line every few seconds.
ballista.history: Crews of the bolt throwers marched with a legion and shot from behind the front ranks.

centurion.name: Centurion
centurion.text: A centurion joins the front. His shout stuns enemies around him.
centurion.history: A centurion led about 80 men and carried a vine stick to beat order into them.

pilum.name: Pilum volley
pilum.text: Legionaries throw pila at the nearest enemies every few seconds.
pilum.history: The pilum's soft iron shank bent on impact, so the enemy could not throw it back.
pilum.more: More pila, thrown more often, that hit harder and pass through.

fire_arrows.name: Burning arrows
fire_arrows.text: Arrows set enemies alight for three seconds.
fire_arrows.history: Arrows wrapped in burning tow were used to set fire to wooden palisades and siege works.

scorpio.name: Scorpio
scorpio.text: A bolt thrower shoots the strongest enemy in range, through everyone in its way.
scorpio.history: The scorpio was a small, precise bolt thrower that could pierce armour at long range.

onager.name: Onager
onager.text: Stones land in the thickest crowd and scatter it.
onager.history: Named after the wild ass for its kick, the onager hurled stones from a twisted-rope arm.

caltrops.name: Caltrops
caltrops.text: Spikes are left behind as the legion marches.
caltrops.history: Iron caltrops always land with a spike pointing up, and were scattered to cripple horses.

stakes.name: Ditch and stakes
stakes.text: A ring of stakes around the legion hurts enemies who cross it.
stakes.history: Roman camps were ringed with a ditch and sharpened stakes, dug fresh every night.
stakes.more: A wider ring that hurts more.

fire_pots.name: Fire pots
fire_pots.text: Jars thrown ahead leave burning ground.
fire_pots.history: Clay pots of pitch and oil were thrown to burst into flames among packed enemy ranks.

war_dogs.name: War dogs
war_dogs.text: Hounds run down enemies who break away.
war_dogs.history: Both sides in the northern wars used big dogs to harry stragglers and guard the camps.

trumpets.name: Trumpets
trumpets.text: A blast every few seconds pushes enemies back.
trumpets.history: Brass tubae and curved cornua sounded every order, from the march to the charge.
trumpets.more: A louder blast, sounded more often.

eagle.name: Eagle
eagle.text: The aquila flashes and strikes every enemy around the commander.
eagle.history: The legion's golden eagle was its soul, and legions fought hard to win a lost one back.
eagle.more: A wider flash that strikes harder.

oil_jars.name: Oil jars
oil_jars.text: Slick ground slows the enemies who cross it.
oil_jars.history: Olive oil was easy to find in any Roman supply train, and a spill made footing treacherous.

torches.name: Torches
torches.history: Marching columns carried torches for night work, and they also set tents and huts alight.

hooked_pila.name: Hooked pila
hooked_pila.text: Pila that hook in and pin enemies in place.
hooked_pila.history: Barbed pila snagged in shields and flesh, so a foe had to drop his shield to be free.

greek_fire.name: Greek fire
greek_fire.text: Burning arrows and fire pots become a fire water cannot put out.
greek_fire.history: Roman-era fire weapons of pitch and naphtha kept burning on water, and their recipes were kept secret.

siege_train.name: Siege train
siege_train.text: Scorpii and onagers fire together as one siege train.
siege_train.history: Roman armies built siege engines on the spot, from timber cut and joined by the soldiers.

hunting_horn.name: Hunting horn
hunting_horn.text: The trumpets call the dogs, who hunt as a pack.
hunting_horn.history: Horns calling the pack to the chase were just as useful for driving a hunted enemy.

burning_eagle.name: Burning eagle
burning_eagle.text: The eagle blazes, and the torches burn with it.
burning_eagle.history: A standard set alight would be a terrible omen, and a rallying cry for those who saw it.

fortified_camp.name: Fortified camp
fortified_camp.text: Stakes and oil turn the legion's ground into a fortified camp.
fortified_camp.history: Every night a legion built a walled camp, and the plan was the same from Britain to Syria.

lorica.name: Lorica
lorica.text: Every soldier has 20% more health, and is healed by as much.

shield_wall.name: Shield wall
shield_wall.text: The front rank takes 10% less damage.

reach.name: Long reach
reach.text: Coins are picked up from 30% further away.

close_order.name: Close order
close_order.text: Soldiers keep their places faster when the formation turns.

testudo.name: Testudo practice
testudo.text: The testudo recharges 2 seconds sooner and holds 1 second longer.

plunder.name: Plunder
plunder.text: Every fallen barbarian drops 15% more denarii.

veterans.name: Veterans
veterans.text: Whenever the legion kills, every soldier gains a little health.

reserves.name: Reserves
reserves.text: A fallen soldier is replaced after 20 seconds, and sooner with each pick.

fortune.name: Fortune
fortune.text: A fourth choice at every level-up.

barbarian_club.name: Club warrior
barbarian_club.text: A warrior of the forest tribes, armed with a heavy club.
barbarian_club.history: Many Germanic warriors owned no armour at all and fought with whatever weapon they could make.

barbarian_spear.name: Spearman
barbarian_spear.text: He keeps just out of a sword's reach, and does not tire.
barbarian_spear.history: The framea, a short spear, was the Germanic warrior's main weapon, used in a thrust or a throw.

axe_thrower.name: Axe thrower
axe_thrower.text: He stops at a distance and throws hand axes at the legion.
axe_thrower.history: Throwing axes were common in Germanic war bands, and were thrown just before closing in.

wolf.name: Wolf
wolf.text: The tribes' wolves run fast and bite hard.
wolf.history: Wolves were sacred to many Germanic tribes, and warriors wore wolf pelts into battle.

berserker.name: Berserker
berserker.text: He runs round to the rear, charges, and spins his axes in a ring. Wounded, he flies into a rage.
berserker.history: Germanic warriors who fought in a frenzy, in wolf and bear skins, were said to feel no pain.

war_band_leader.name: War band leader
war_band_leader.text: The leader of a raiding band, who never walks alone. He raises his shield to the legion and calls his band to him.
war_band_leader.history: Germanic warriors fought in family groups behind a chosen leader, who shared the spoils.

war_priest.name: War priest
war_priest.text: He stands back and hurls burning pots into the thickest ranks. He heals the warriors round him, curses the legion and vanishes in smoke when soldiers reach him.
war_priest.history: Germanic priests marched to war alongside the tribes and read the omens before a battle.

chieftain.name: War chief
chieftain.text: The war chief who united the tribes against Rome, swinging a great axe.
chieftain.history: In 9 AD Arminius led three Roman legions into a forest ambush at Teutoburg and destroyed them.

painted_warrior.name: Painted warrior
painted_warrior.text: A warrior painted blue for battle.
painted_warrior.history: Britons were said to dye their bodies blue with woad, to look fearsome in battle.

briton_slinger.name: Slinger
briton_slinger.text: He slings stones from a distance.
briton_slinger.history: Slingers fought across Iron Age Britain, and hillforts kept stockpiles of sling stones.

chariot.name: Chariot
chariot.text: A light chariot that drives straight at the legion.
chariot.history: Britons fought from chariots long after the rest of Europe had given them up.

druid_acolyte.name: Druid acolyte
druid_acolyte.text: A druid in training, who curses the legion from afar.
druid_acolyte.history: Druid trainees spent up to twenty years memorising law and lore, since nothing was written down.

chariot_charge.name: Chariot charge
chariot_charge.history: British charioteers raced along the front line, throwing spears before dropping to fight on foot.

druid.name: Druid
druid.text: An old priest of the oak groves, said to call down fire.
druid.history: The druids were priests, judges and teachers, and Rome attacked their island stronghold at Mona.

warrior_queen.name: Warrior queen
warrior_queen.text: A queen who rides a war chariot against Rome.
warrior_queen.history: In 60 AD Boudica led the Iceni in a revolt that burned Londinium to the ground.

gaul_swordsman.name: Swordsman
gaul_swordsman.text: A Gaulish warrior whose long sword cuts down two men at once.
gaul_swordsman.history: Gaulish long swords were made for slashing, and bent so easily that warriors straightened them.

gaul_horseman.name: Horseman
gaul_horseman.text: He rides along the legion's flank, then rears and strikes with his horse's hooves.
gaul_horseman.history: Gaulish cavalry were among the best in Europe, and Caesar hired many into his own army.

gaul_archer.name: Archer
gaul_archer.text: He shoots high over his own lines, and the arrows fall where a ring marks the ground.
gaul_archer.history: Archers were rarer among the Gauls, who preferred to fight with sword and spear.

boar.name: Boar
boar.text: It charges in a straight line and cannot turn. A hedge or stake in its path stuns it.
boar.history: The boar was a Gaulish sacred animal, and its image topped many a helmet and war standard.

champion.name: Champion
champion.text: He calls out the commander to a ring. Fight him inside it and he falls faster; walk away and he and the warriors round him grow fiercer.
champion.history: Celtic champions fought in front of the line, and challenged enemy heroes to single combat.

horn_blower.name: Horn blower
horn_blower.text: His carnyx speeds and heals the warriors round him, and its blast pushes the ranks back and slows their blows. He runs from soldiers who reach him.
horn_blower.history: The carnyx, a tall bronze horn with an animal head, was meant to terrify the foe.

gaul_king.name: Gaulish king
gaul_king.text: A king with a long sword and a sworn bodyguard: while two of his guards live he takes little harm. He rings the legion with stakes and calls horsemen from the hills.
gaul_king.history: Vercingetorix united the Gauls in 52 BC and held out against Caesar at the siege of Alesia.

falx_warrior.name: Falx warrior
falx_warrior.text: He fights with the falx, a curved blade that cuts through shields.
falx_warrior.history: The falx was a curved two-handed blade that could cut through a Roman helmet.

dacian_archer.name: Archer
dacian_archer.text: A mountain archer with a strong bow.
dacian_archer.history: Dacian archers shot from the high ground of mountain fortresses.

wolf_standard_bearer.name: Wolf-standard bearer
wolf_standard_bearer.text: He carries the wolf-headed dragon standard that howls in the wind.
wolf_standard_bearer.history: The Dacian draco, a wolf-headed dragon standard, howled as the wind passed through it.

mountain_bear.name: Mountain bear
mountain_bear.text: A bear from the high passes.
mountain_bear.history: Brown bears lived in the Carpathian forests, and the Dacians hunted them.

falx_band.name: Falx band
falx_band.text: A band of falx warriors fighting as one.
falx_band.history: After meeting the falx, Roman soldiers added extra armour to their arms and helmets.

priest.name: Priest
priest.text: He speaks for Zalmoxis and heartens the host.
priest.history: Dacian priests had great power at the court, and the king took their advice on war.

dacian_king.name: Dacian king
dacian_king.text: A king who advances behind a moving shield wall.
dacian_king.history: Decebalus held off Rome for years, until Trajan conquered Dacia in 106 AD.

horse_archer.name: Horse archer
horse_archer.text: He rides circles round the legion, firing as he goes.
horse_archer.history: Parthian horsemen would shoot backwards as they rode away, the famous Parthian shot.

cataphract.name: Cataphract
cataphract.text: A rider in full scale armour on an armoured horse.
cataphract.history: Cataphracts were riders in full scale armour, and so were their horses.

camel_rider.name: Camel rider
camel_rider.text: A rider whose camel frightens the legion's horses.
camel_rider.history: Camels carried desert armies over ground that stopped most other horses and mules.

parthian_slinger.name: Slinger
parthian_slinger.text: He slings lead shot from the dunes.
parthian_slinger.history: Slingers in the Parthian armies fought alongside the archers to thin out an advancing force.

cataphract_charge.name: Cataphract charge
cataphract_charge.text: A wall of armoured horsemen at full gallop.
cataphract_charge.history: A cataphract charge could break an infantry line, as it did at Carrhae.

war_elephant.name: War elephant
war_elephant.text: It tramples whatever stands before it.
war_elephant.history: Eastern kings used war elephants to scare horses and to break the ranks of foot soldiers.

shah.name: Shah
shah.text: The shah of Parthia, riding into battle on an elephant.
shah.history: In 53 BC at Carrhae, the Parthian army crushed seven Roman legions led by Crassus.

germania.name: Germania
germania.text: Dark forests and clearings, where whole legions have vanished.

britannia.name: Britannia
britannia.text: Wet moorland at the edge of the known world.

tribune.name: Tribune
tribune.text: A young officer with two legionaries at his side.
tribune.history: Young men of good family served as tribunes to learn command, and wore a purple stripe.

archer_captain.name: Archer captain
archer_captain.history: Auxiliary archer units were led by a Roman prefect who knew the bow and the ground.

cavalry_prefect.name: Cavalry prefect
cavalry_prefect.text: He starts with two cavalrymen and marches faster.
cavalry_prefect.history: A prefect of cavalry commanded an ala, a wing of about 500 horsemen on the flank.

engineer.name: Engineer
engineer.history: Legions carried their own engineers, and Roman roads and bridges were built by soldiers.

old_centurion.name: Old centurion
old_centurion.text: He starts with a centurion, has more health and marches slower.
old_centurion.history: A senior centurion could serve for decades, and the best earned the rank of primus pilus.

legate.name: Legate
legate.text: He starts with a standard bearer and a free reroll.
legate.history: A legate commanded a full legion of about 5,000 men, and was often a senator.

start_health.name: Starting health
start_health.text: The commander begins with more health.

start_soldiers.name: Starting soldiers
start_soldiers.text: The legion begins with more soldiers.

pickup_radius.name: Pickup radius
pickup_radius.text: Coins are picked up from further away.

rerolls.name: Rerolls
rerolls.text: More rerolls of the level-up choices in each run.

banishes.name: Banishes
banishes.text: Remove a choice from the run's pool for good.

recruit_cap.name: Barracks
recruit_cap.text: The legion can hold more soldiers.

level_ease.name: Veteran standards
level_ease.text: Fewer coins are needed for each level.

choice_luck.name: Haruspex
choice_luck.text: Arms and recruits come up more often at level-ups.

triumphal_arch.name: Triumphal arch
triumphal_arch.text: Raise an arch to the legion's victories in the camp, one stage at a time.

triumph.name: Hold a triumph
triumph.text: Parade through the finished arch. Each triumph sets up another gilded statue.

win_as_archer_captain.name: Victory as the Archer captain
win_as_archer_captain.text: Win a run as the Archer captain.

win_as_engineer.name: Victory as the Engineer
win_as_engineer.text: Win a run as the Engineer.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.text: A storm of lightning strikes down the barbarians on screen.
jupiter.history: Jupiter Optimus Maximus, king of the gods, held the thunderbolt and guarded Rome from the Capitoline Hill.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.text: An earthquake throws every barbarian on screen back and stuns them.
neptune.history: Neptune ruled the sea and shook the earth, and Romans blamed him for earthquakes.

mars.name: Mars
mars.text: War frenzy: triple damage, faster blows and half the harm for 10 seconds.
mars.history: Mars, father of Romulus, was the god of war; legions swore to him before a campaign.

vulcan.name: Vulcan
vulcan.text: Fire rains on the screen: every barbarian burns and the ground catches fire.
vulcan.history: Vulcan forged weapons in fires under the mountains; Romans held his feast to keep Rome safe from fire.

apollo.name: Apollo
apollo.text: Golden light heals the whole legion and brings back up to 10 fallen soldiers.
apollo.history: Apollo, god of light and healing, was given a temple in Rome to end a plague in 433 BC.

free_choice_note: A free choice from a chest or cart heals the legion instead when there is nothing left to offer.
